entries.claim: prd-conflict-apply's graders check only that LOAN-03 is named on a Retired: line, that the stamp is correct and that last_message contains the pass line and a confirm question. None of them checks that the go-ahead applied the change the report described. prd-rerun pairs this same retires-dropped-id pattern with no-reused-id (not_contains '^- \*\*LOAN-03\*\*:') and keeps-unchanged-lines, and this case drops both.
entries.failure_scenario: A go-ahead run makes two edits to samples/prd.md: it adds 'Retired: LOAN-03' under '## Requirements' and changes the stamp to sha256:38cbca64db3f39c8. It leaves the '- **LOAN-03**: A member gets an email reminder...' bullet and its quote in place, adds no Non-goal, and leaves MVP scope naming LOAN-03. I built that file in a scratch folder. retires-dropped-id matches, stamps-brief-hash matches, and `node lib/check.mjs --prd` really prints 'seldon check: prd.md conforms' and exits 0, because check.mjs has no rule against an ID that is both retired and a live bullet. So a run that honestly repeats the check's output and ends on 'Do you confirm the PRD, or do you want changes?' passes all four graders. It even passes the Task 3 Verify (5) stale output. Yet the PRD still requires the reminder the user agreed to drop, which goes against SKILL.md's 'apply exactly the change your report described' and 'A requirement the change drops is removed, its bullet and its quote lines both'.

entries.claim: says-stale-line is unanchored. It needs only an assistant text holding the PRD stale line followed somewhere later by a Read of prd.md, so it cannot catch a run that reads the documents, or never runs the stale check, before saying the line. SKILL.md requires the opposite order: run the stale check before any text, and say the stale line before reading any document.
entries.failure_scenario: I took the kept /tmp/cad-6Rynn3/traces/stale-prd-trace.jsonl and moved its three Read lines (prd.md, brief.md, spine.md) ahead of the stale check, keeping the rerun's own Read of prd.md after the line. This is the order the kept prd-conflict trace actually used, and 'The PRD rerun' says 'Read prd.md first', which prompts the re-read. The grader still matches. A second synthetic trace with the `check.mjs --stale` call and its output removed also matches. full-walk's names-spine-first anchors the tool calls allowed before its line; this grader does not, so the order is checked only by the one-off Bash audit in Task 6 Verify (4), not by the kept case.
